Looking back she probably still thinks something way creepier happened than the ass beating i got with my first 2 quarters.

I do too. the mall I used to go to with my mom doesnt even have an arcade anymore. Or the 2 or 3  music/video stores it used to have. Or the 2 or 3 toy stores. My kids can't experience a mall the way I did and it makes me a little sad. They wont look at it as the neat experience that I did and eventually turn into the mallrat that I was at 16-17. 

The mall does still have a Sbarro Pizza though so I guess thats something. that pizza is still bangin.

This is a thought I have had for a long time. I had a teacher a long time ago who really drilled home prejudice and how it lies at the heart of racism. One being simply prejudging another based on limited information. Skin color, the place you grew up, what clothes you wear. Racism is pre judging, and so are these other things, but that doesnt mean all prejudice is racism. I actually really disliked this teacher because I was a little shit and she didnt take shit at all; but damn if I dont remember what she told us and look back on her differently now that time has passed.

I would take such a stat and say that it's a result of societal/cultural norms. The Inuit are in a far different climate with polar opposite requirements for survival. Running in a severely cold environment is just a colossal waste of calories. The Inuit, and most mammals in that environment, have to practice conservation of energy. They have to use the least amount of calories possible to get food so that they can endure the extended periods of scarcity. 

The Inuit culture is driven by more of a gathering and enduring mentality comprised of fishing and trapping. Low calorie actions. Africans also gather plants but expend far more energy in hunting due to having to track and stalk prey, subsequently covering longer distances. High calorie actions.

However none of that is to say that an Inuit cannot survive or is incapable of running long distances like a native African. They simply arent trained to excel in that environment. Given time, I'm sure they can. Just like an  African predisposed to a different food-gathering approach could learn to excel in a severe-cold environment if they are given the time to acclimate.
